records.quote: Example 3 (Inverse Gamma distribution). The density function of the inverse Gamma distribution with parameters α, β ∈ R++ is f (x) = β α x−α−1 exp (−β/x) /Γ(α), x ∈ R++ . By Remark 2, if α ≤ 1 and β ∈ R++ , we have F ∈ H. The inverse Gamma distribution with α = 0.5 is the Lévy distribution, which also belongs to the class of stable distributions.

records.quote: Proposition 1. The following statements hold. (i) If random variable X satisfies (SD), then either X is a constant, or E[|X|] is infinite. (ii) If two independent random variables X and Y satisfy (SD), then X + Y satisfies (SD). (iii) If random variable X satisfies (SD), then (X + a)/b satisfies (SD) for all a ∈ R and b ∈ R++ . (iv) If random variable Yk with any k ∈ N satisfies (SD) and Yk →d X, then X satisfies (SD).
records.model: other: linear combinations of iid random variables
records.compared: preservation/closure of the (SD) ordering relation; (i) is a necessary structural condition

records.quote: As the absolute Cauchy distribution satisfies (SD), a natural question is whether absolute stable distributions with parameter α ≤ 1 also satisfy (SD). We conjecture that the answer is yes but do not have a proof. We use the stochastic representation of stable random variables in Weron (1996) to simulate 10000 random samples of two independent stable random variables X1 , X2 ∼ Sα (1, β, 0); ... Let Y1 = a1 |X1 | + a2 |X2 | and Y2 = b1 |X1 | + b2 |X2 |. We consider three cases of the weight vector (a1 , a2 , b1 , b2 ) = (1, 4, 2, 3), (2, 6, 3, 5) or (3, 8, 5, 6). ... the empirical distributions Fb1 and Fb2 of Y1 and Y2 seem to satisfy Fb1 (x) ≥ Fb2 (x) for all x.
records.model: other: linear combinations of absolute values of iid stable variables
records.compared: Y1 = a·|X| vs Y2 = b·|X| with a more spread than b (e.g., (1,4) vs (2,3))

conclusion.direction: empirical cdfs satisfy F̂1(x) ≥ F̂2(x) for all x, i.e., Y1 ≤st Y2 — taken as support for the conjecture that |Sα| with α ≤ 1 satisfies (SD)

records.ambiguity: Simulation evidence only — an explicit conjecture, not a theorem. Printed symbols 'Fb1/Fb2' are the empirical cdfs F̂1, F̂2 of Y1, Y2. Under the conjectured (SD), the more spread weight vector a gives the smaller sum: Y1 ≤st Y2, matching the printed F̂1 ≥ F̂2.

note: Same printed claim as the 'absolute stable conjecture' queue item; one canonical record kept identical.
